summary: Round-5 verify of the two findings against rounds:M4.43. R4b is FIXED: the round labels are gone, the reason is stated, and the remaining ordinal ('the final round') is the one thing left of it -- filed below as a minor. R4a is HALF fixed. The test-reviewer half is now exactly what the record says: TR-M4.17-3 (.harness/review/e8a3151c...test-reviewer.json) reads 'fastRate = 4, 3, 4, 4, 3 over five class-scoped runs -- failures 0, 1, 0, 0, 1 -- plus two full :sequencer:test runs (246 tests) at 1 failure then 0. Killed in 3 of 7 runs' and 'honest never went below 6 in seven runs, including at load 123', and 'bimodal at 3/4' is verbatim. The new attributions elsewhere in the line also check out: the `3L to be less than 3L` red is TR-M4.43-1 (961791a8...test-reviewer.json), the PRODUCTION third copy is M4.43-R1b (68c71440...reviewer.json), the drainPermits loss is M4.43-R1a. The production half does not: no verdict in .harness/review records a production retraction, and production's last recorded word on that question still asserts the opposite. I grepped every verdict mentioning multipliedBy(2), every occurrence of 'retract' in .harness/review, and every copy of these claims in baselines/ and the three backlog files -- the retraction claim exists in exactly one copy, so this is not a duplicate-survives case, it is the surviving half of the clause R4a flagged.

findings.title: The sentence rewritten to be 'ATTRIBUTED PER ROLE AND ONLY AS THE RECORD SUPPORTS IT' still ends on a production retraction no verdict records -- and production's last recorded word says the opposite, uncorrected
findings.summary: 'THE PRODUCTION REVIEWER re-measured independently and RETRACTED its own earlier report that the floor fix held.' Half of that is supported: production did re-measure (M4.43-R1d, 68c71440...reviewer.json: 'I measured the same configuration in my own tree ... and got fast=6, fast=7, fast=7'), and production does have its own earlier report that the floor fix held (e8a3151c...reviewer.json, round-4 summary: 'the raised rate floor kills multipliedBy(2) -- the mutant lands at exactly 3 against isBetween(4L,30L), while the honest run measured 7 three times at load average 186, so the floor keeps 1.75x slack'). The RETRACTION is not there. I grepped 'retract' across every file in .harness/review and read every production verdict for M4.17 and M4.43 (2034bc4b, eaae807c, 6e0d2ee2, e8a3151c, 68c71440, 0d447714, b0a1c839, 57281fcd): none of them withdraws that claim. Worse for the entry than absence: e8a3151c's two verdicts were recorded 05:38 (test-reviewer, 'THE FLOOR OF 4 DOES NOT KILL multipliedBy(2); it kills it about 40% of the time') and 05:40 (reviewer, 'the raised rate floor kills multipliedBy(2)'). Production recorded its claim two minutes AFTER the contradicting measurement and it stands in the permanent record uncorrected, so the two roles disagreed at one hash and were never reconciled -- which is a more interesting fact than a retraction and is the one the record actually supports. R4a's point (4) had already said this attribution was the test reviewer's; the rewrite kept the clause and changed only the roles around it. The same standard was applied unevenly one clause apart: the twelve-run production series was dropped because no verdict carries it, while this claim, which also no verdict carries, was kept inside the sentence that promises 'ONLY AS THE RECORD SUPPORTS IT'. If the retraction was said in a reviewer's prose report rather than recorded, M0.64 (backlog-notes.md:45) is the tree's own ruling on that: 'A REVIEWER CAN REPORT A VERDICT IT NEVER RECORDED' -- 'reported' and 'recorded' can disagree and only the recorded one is a fact.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.15 (M4's VERIFIED.md and milestone review) is the next open row and reads both baselines/review.txt and .harness. It reads 'THE PRODUCTION REVIEWER ... RETRACTED', greps .harness/review for the retraction, and finds instead a production verdict at e8a3151c that still says the floor kills multipliedBy(2) -- so it cannot tell whether the entry is false or a verdict was lost, in the one file whose worth is that its entries are checkable, in the commit filing three rows about claims stated without being run. It also mis-teaches the escape it exists to record: the reader concludes the roles converged on the measurement, when what the record shows is that they contradicted each other at one hash and only the test role's number survives -- which is exactly the state M4.41 is filed to fix. Non-negotiable 4, one entry below rounds:M4.17, which already records the same error twice.
findings.remedy: One clause, no redraft: replace 'RETRACTED its own earlier report that the floor fix held' with what production actually recorded -- 'three runs at a 2000ms window: 6, 7, 7' -- or state the disagreement plainly: production's own round-4 report that the floor kills the mutant was recorded two minutes after the test review that measured it surviving, and stands uncorrected.

findings.title: The one ordinal left after the round numbers were removed is stale: 'the final round passed both roles' describes a round that two further rounds followed, one of them with a major on this line
findings.summary: '⚠️ THIS ENTRY CLAIMS NO CONVERGENCE: the final round passed both roles and still returned two new minors, both introduced by the previous round's fixes and both the same counting shape.' The round it describes is b0a1c839 (both roles pass, R3a and R3b, both counting-shape, both introduced by the fix to R2a) -- the attribution to 'the previous round's fixes' is now correct, which R4b asked for. 'Final' is not: 57281fcd (reviewer, changes-requested, major M4.43-R4a against this very line) came after it, and this round is after that. Either reading fails -- as a claim about b0a1c839 it is contradicted by .harness, and as a claim about the round that will land the commit it asserts an outcome not yet observed. The fix for R4b removed the numbering on the ground that hand-carried round labels go stale; this file already states that principle at rounds:M4.7a ('the count is left to review_rounds.py, because a count carried by hand in prose is stale by the round after it'), and 'the final round' is the same hand-carried ordinal, stale by the round after it.
findings.failure_scenario: Bounded, and named as minor for the reason R4b was: the do-not-split argument holds under any ordering and the authoritative round count comes from review_rounds.py, so no session is sent to do wrong work. The cost is on the reader of the permanent record, who reconciles 'the final round passed both roles' with a changes-requested verdict recorded after it and has to open .harness to learn which sentence to believe -- in the paragraph whose subject is that counting is what goes stale. Fixing it is permitted and probably wrong at round 6; if it is fixed, the smallest form is 'a round late in the sequence passed both roles', which cannot go stale.
findings.remedy: Drop 'final', or record it in the commit body and land.
